name: Quando Quango
label: Factory Records
lede: A Haçienda booker and a Dutch synth player made a handful of Factory twelve-inches that Larry Levan played at the Paradise Garage, and that a Chicago teenager heard before house music had a name.

eras.title: A Mancunian in Rotterdam
eras.text: Mike Pickering followed a girl to the Netherlands and came back with a band. Quando Quango started in Rotterdam as Latin, jazz, reggae and disco run through a new wave filter, and moved to Manchester just as the Haçienda opened.

years.src: Dream Machines · Factory Benelux · Tim Lawrence
years.h: Pickering moves to Rotterdam and recruits a piano player
years.p: Pickering met Gonnie Rietveld on a holiday on a Dutch island and moved to Rotterdam to be with her. She played piano, which was enough for him; her brother Reinier played drums.
years.xp:
Rietveld remembers the pitch as "You can play piano, that will do." She bought her first synthesizer with money from her father's estate.

Wikipedia and Factory Benelux date the start to 1980; Tim Lawrence's Haçienda history says 1979.

years.h: In a squatted waterworks, Pickering puts on New Order
years.p: Pickering squatted a disused water works in Rotterdam and DJed at a night called Rotterdam Must Dance. He says he put on the second [[New Order|f1106b17-dcbb-45f6-b938-199ccfab50cc]] gig after [[Ian Curtis|10ae1bf6-88b2-4fb4-8fbe-8227a49803d3]] died.

years.src: Factory Benelux · Tim Lawrence · Red Bull Music Academy
years.h: Rob Gretton hears the demo and the band moves to Manchester
years.p: Pickering, an old friend of New Order's manager [[Rob Gretton|41b55fab-da3b-4ecf-a67d-aeeec338a9c5]], joined the team opening the Haçienda, booking its bands and DJs.
years.xp: "I used to book the DJs, lighting, bands, everything," Pickering told Red Bull Music Academy.

years.p: The debut twelve-inch, with 'Tingle' on the other side. Factory Benelux calls it a double-sided EP.

years.h: Pickering gets a young band called [[James|a2accb58-6099-4cb5-a3c8-f6332f364db5]] onto a Haçienda bill
years.p: On his recommendation James played the Haçienda with New Order, [[The Durutti Column|aaddb5e3-f8a5-4a9d-8674-f885112ecf0e]] and [[Section 25|82e26f64-813d-4b22-a442-44d182f7f9eb]]. Tony Wilson saw the film of the show and offered them a deal.

eras.title: Big at the Garage
eras.text: 'Love Tempo' went to New York for a remix and came back an underground club record. For a few years a Factory band from Manchester had a following on the dance floors that were inventing what came next.

years.src: Wikipedia: Quando Quango · Dream Machines · Tim Lawrence
years.p: [[Bernard Sumner|6fa2e161-200e-475a-8492-3755594581f9]] co-produced and played keyboards; [[A Certain Ratio|73577e86-4da8-4d76-949d-34c757e053be]]'s [[Donald Johnson|49569ee1-aba3-4c08-8ead-9791a7f8c96d]] played guitar and bass. [[Mark Kamins|bf7d6db4-a395-4f1e-b44a-3c097d951ebc]]'s New York mix made it a club record, No. 4 on Billboard's dance chart.
years.xp:
"We recorded it in spring, and then it went to New York for a remix," Rietveld says. Kamins was a DJ at New York's Danceteria.

Years later, researching her PhD in Chicago, Rietveld found house producer Vince Lawrence citing 'Love Tempo' as something that inspired him when he heard it at 16.

years.cap: Quando Quango on a New York street, 1983
years.src: Tim Lawrence · Red Bull Music Academy
years.h: Larry Levan's Paradise Garage books Quando Quango for a live PA
years.p: [[Larry Levan|3522a104-c3ce-4ee8-865a-fcf3fc08095d]] loved 'Love Tempo', so the band played the Garage. In New York they also warmed up for New Order.
years.xp: Pickering came home changed by the Garage and by Kamins's eclectic sets at Danceteria. Both shaped what he did next at the Haçienda.

yt: Live at the ICA, London, Oct 1983
years.h: Simon Topping leaves A Certain Ratio for the percussion
years.p: Reinier Rietveld left for his band Spasmodique. [[Simon Topping|6dd95305-7ca6-464d-a9de-93c3a963cda9]] came in on percussion; Derek Johnson played bass, then his brother Barry Johnson, from Sweet Sensation and later [[Aswad|617f2574-c2bd-4e39-9627-34fc9742a024]], took over.

years.h: Johnny Marr plays on 'Atom Rock', and meets Sumner
years.p: [[Johnny Marr|ff621094-2a76-401f-8398-b75b5fd2be24]] of [[The Smiths|40f5d9e4-2de7-4f2d-ad41-e31a9a9fea27]] added guitar to a Quando Quango track Sumner was producing. Five years later the two of them were [[Electronic|3cdb360e-d0a2-459f-92f6-f0f28e62127d]].

years.cap: City Life magazine feature with Gonnie Rietveld, Manchester, 1984
years.h: Kamins produces the album at Strawberry Studios, Stockport
years.p: The sessions were mixed in New York at Shakedown and in England at Genetik.

eras.title: An album, a club night, a split
eras.text: The one album came out as Pickering was turning the Haçienda into a dance club. The band itself didn't make it through 1986.

years.cap: The Hit magazine on Quando Quango, posed in front of a 'Genius' poster, 1985
years.h: 'Genius', FAC 137, goes out as a party twelve-inch
years.p: It reached No. 38 on the UK indie chart.

years.h: An Imamura film gives FACT 110 its name
years.p: Pigs + Battleships borrows the title of Shohei Imamura's 1961 film. Marr and [[Vini Reilly|f639c53e-c709-407f-9711-de495461f28d]] of the Durutti Column guest; it reached No. 17 on the indie chart.
years.xp:
Kevin Cummins took the cover photographs. Andy Connell and Beverley McDonald are on it too.

LTM reissued it on CD in 2003 with the singles and B-sides; Factory Benelux added BBC sessions for its 2013 edition.

years.cap: Poster for New Order with Quando Quango at the Manhattan Club, Leuven, December 1985
q: One thousand six hundred people in a one thousand two hundred capacity club
years.h: Pickering launches Nude and the Haçienda fills up
years.p: Pickering and Marc Berry started the Friday night, playing soul, hip hop, electro and Motown.
years.xp: He told Tim Lawrence it took two or three weeks to get there.

years.cap: Manchester Evening News piece on Quando Quango at G-Mex, 1986
years.h: Lisa Stansfield sings; Stephen Morris drums
years.p: [[Lisa Stansfield|8f632c44-c97f-4b12-b1cd-caf2c6e2ed06]] and New Order's [[Stephen Morris|b3036249-8b39-4d02-a312-d31a63497bbc]] guested on 1986 sessions. Morris's percussion part later turned into the [[M People|f6f69dba-4c49-4f1b-a6bc-678c1154f32d]] track 'Kiss It Better'.

years.h: 'Bad Blood', FAC 156, is shelved when the band ends
years.p: Late demos of 'Bad Blood' and 'Vision of America' went unreleased; 'What Price Beauty' came from the last session.
years.xp: Rietveld has said the end came alongside her father's death, the breakdown of her marriage and the strain of the move to Manchester.

eras.title: Dance happened anyway
eras.text: Pickering kept going toward house: T-Coy, M People, a long career in A&R. Rietveld went into academia and ended up writing the history her band was part of.

years.h: Pickering and Gretton pitch Tony Wilson a dance label
years.p: Wilson's answer, as Pickering tells it, around 1986 or 1987. Pickering later signed Black Box, Felix and Guru Josh to Deconstruction.

years.h: Pickering and Topping make 'Carino' as T-Coy
years.p: Tim Lawrence calls it the first notable UK house record.

years.src: Red Bull Music Academy · Wikipedia: Mike Pickering
years.h: M People win the Mercury Prize
years.p: Pickering wrote, produced and played saxophone live in [[M People|f6f69dba-4c49-4f1b-a6bc-678c1154f32d]], his band after Quando Quango.

years.h: LTM brings back 'Love Tempo' in the Kamins mix
years.p: The reissue twelve-inch paired it with 'Genius' and an 'Atom Rock' dub. That year Rietveld set up music and sound design studies at London South Bank University, where she became Professor of Sonic Culture.
